status: FAILED — reproduced; root cause not yet proven
scope: Physical Digitakt mk1 OS 1.54 I04R + Pi 4B 128-frame kernel, one USB1 voice on track 1; disposable project; speakers lowered

rows.human_observation: DEP control became very sluggish above about 32, regardless of speed; Play lagged several seconds; Stop took about 8 seconds to take effect. Repeated with trace on and voice muted: same encoder lag, multi-second parameter response, and about 7-second Play/Stop delay.
rows.interpretation: The failure reproduces with the Pi voice muted and no Pi playout fault, new FIFO underrun, or USB gap/error. It is therefore device-side control/UI service contention or a Digitakt CPU-load effect, not a Pi audio deadline failure. This supports the human's CPU-overtasking hypothesis but does not yet prove which native task/path is starved.

stop_decision: Stopped at first UI/transport failure per preregistered rules. No S3/S4 rows were run.

instrumentation_limit.fifo_rise_cause: Isolated to the trace dump: FIFO was 12 through 00:10:00, then the next engine row reported a 3003 us control pass and FIFO 0/63. This is an instrumentation side effect, not counted as part of the UI-failure interval.

evidence_classes.physical_measurement: Pi counters, USB telemetry, FIFO, playout faults, retained trace
evidence_classes.human_observation: DEP/encoder sluggishness, Play/Stop delays, audio continuity
evidence_classes.source_fact: trxtrace forces mute; final SRC values come from the render hook
evidence_classes.hypothesis: Digitakt native control/service or CPU is overtasked by dense effective updates; exact path unproven

limitations: No precise DEP threshold was measured; human estimate is above about +32 and possibly symmetric near -32
The 128-row trace covers only about133 ms, so it cannot establish the cause of the multi-second UI stall
No native CPU/task timing instrument was captured during the stall
No calibrated UI latency measurement exists; delays are human-observed seconds
The FIFO rise after the trace dump is excluded from the failure interval but leaves a higher baseline for later runs
next_action: Phase 2 device-side isolation: capture native task/IRQ service timing and effective-update cadence over a multi-second stall, then test whether the capture/control worker is starving the UI task. Do not attribute the cause to Pi playback or adopt a larger buffer/coalescing workaround before that evidence exists.
